newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica to alter monetary goals due to slowdown.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica to alter monetary goals due to slowdown.

text.p: Costa Rica Central Bank President Rodrigo Bolanos said Monday the government would revise the goals of country's monetary policy to reflect the Costa Rica's economic slowdown.

Bolanos said the Central Bank now is aiming for a 12.5 percent inflation in 1996, up from the previous goal of 10 percent; a current accounts deficit of 0.8 percent, down from the previously expected 2.0 percent; and a net international reserve goal of $900 million to $950 million, down from $1.1 billion.

He said the goals are based on estimated GDP growth of 1 percent for 1996, down from the previous projection 3.0 percent, and a public-sector deficit of 3.0 percent of GDP, compared to the previous projection of 0.8 percent.

The Central Bank recently released figures showing that the Costa Rican economy contracted in each of the first six months of the year compared to the same months of the year before, shrinking by 2.5 percent in each April and May and then contracting another 2.0 percent in June.

Bolanos attributed the slowdown in part to banks' high interest rates of more than 32 percent that prevailed last. Interest rates have since dropped and will fluctuate between 22 percent and 24 percent for the rest of the year, he said.
Rates for private sector credit, the rate at which the government lends to private institutions, were adjusted down to 15 percent from 18 percent because of the continued slowdown, Bolanos said.
He said the Central Bank's monetary policy aims to allow for economic recovery without introducing inflationary or balance of payments pressures.
